## Purpose
Create, read, update and delete Mistral document libraries (Libraries API) and their documents, including webpage import. Deleting also cleans the matching knowledge-graph data.

## Responsibilities
| Endpoint | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `GET /libraries` | `library_service.list_libraries()` |
| `POST /libraries` | body `{name, description=""}` |
| `PUT /libraries/{id}` | body `{name?, description?}` |
| `DELETE /libraries/{id}` | refused with 409 while any agent has the library attached (`delete_rules.check_library_deletable` raises `InUse`); then deletes it and adds `graph: delete_rules.forget_in_graph("library", id)` |
| `GET /libraries/{id}/documents` | list the documents |
| `POST /libraries/{id}/documents` | multipart upload (filename defaults to "untitled", content type to octet-stream) |
| `POST /libraries/{id}/documents/webpage` | body `{url}`: fetch the page and upload it as a document |
| `DELETE /libraries/{id}/documents/{doc}` | delete it and add `graph: forget_library_document_in_graph(...)` |

## Key elements
See Responsibilities.

## Control flow
None.

## Data, state and side effects
- Calls Mistral's Libraries API.
- Writes Neo4j and the annotation tables during cleanup.

## Configuration
None.

## Interactions
- Route policy: knowledge.view for GET and knowledge.manage for writes.
- Graph RAG ingestion is in `routes/rag.py` and `app/rag`.

## Error handling and edge cases
Every service failure is turned into 500 "Failed to <action>: <error>".

## Nuances and gotchas
Deleting a document used to leave its entities in Neo4j, where an unscoped lookup could still cite a document nobody can open. The graph cleanup on delete was added to fix that.

## How to rebuild this file
Eight handlers and three body models, as described.
